prospect.name: Robert Belanger
prospect.location: New England, USA — has a specialist appointment in Boston the following day; exact city not stated
prospect.occupation: Retired police officer. Served 32 years and retired in 2021; was the department's wellness coordinator and ran morning bootcamp classes for officers. Now works per-diem road and safety details for the department, roughly one job a week, to supplement his income. Describes himself as on a fixed income.
prospect.family_status: Girlfriend of 16 years. One son turning 30 in July, living independently, no grandchildren yet. A brother four years younger whose health has deteriorated badly. His father retired at 60, declined, and spent the last ten years of his life in a wheelchair before dying at 82.
prospect.training_background: Lifelong trainer, self-described as addicted to working out. Holds personal training certifications obtained while serving, and ran department bootcamp classes using kettlebells, battle ropes, push-ups and calisthenics. Currently trains three to five times a week with bands, kettlebells, dumbbells and machines plus a lot of walking, sometimes carrying a kettlebell. Has a home gym with kettlebells, bands and a pull-up tower. First introduced to kettlebells about fifteen years ago; does swings and goblet squats and wants to learn the more technical movements such as the windmill. Cannot use barbells. Was benching 400 lb at 25. Skis through the winter. Currently 210 lb at 5'9", down from 220, targeting 200. Follows Trevor's social feeds and trains off them.
prospect.medical: Extensive and partly unresolved. Two back surgeries resulting in an L3-L4-L5 spinal fusion; reports retaining good hip mobility. Struck by a car on duty in 2003 while working a drunk-driver stop, requiring ulnar nerve surgery, after which clinicians told him 'your lifting days are over' — this is why he abandoned barbell training. Roughly two years ago he fell on the way to the gym and tore his triceps; the long head has not recovered and he has a specialist appointment in Boston the following day to investigate why. Prostate issues causing repeated night waking. Self-reported declining testosterone; takes some supplements but no steroids or TRT. Sleep is a stated problem — targets seven hours, in bed around 9pm, awake by 5 or 6am.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Offered only as a possibility and never specified. 'most of the clients take it upfront. For certain clients, I don't feel that this is the best thing for their situation, so we can break it up.' When asked directly what the options were, the rep answered 'We don't have anything set in stone. It always differs from the particular person' and made the disclosure of options conditional on the prospect first disclosing his finances. No figure, term or schedule was ever named.

evidence: Four explicit declines, escalating in firmness: 'That's something I'd have to sleep on', 'Maybe it's just not the right time for me', 'I'm just going to decline at this time. I'm going to decline', and 'I don't think it's for me right now. I'm sorry.'
Stated affordability constraint with specifics — existing debts to clear, a fixed income, and unwillingness to take on financing.
Refused to disclose his financial position when asked: 'I just don't want to disclose that information to you. That's personal.'
No payment taken, no link sent, no structure ever put on the table.

Counter-evidence: he never wavered on wanting the programme. When asked whether he was still positive on it after the price landed he said 'Yeah, oh yeah', and confirmed money was the sole barrier — 'No, that's it. That's it. It's all about the money.'
Counter-evidence: he indicated a future window — his current debts 'will be paid up in a matter of months, and then I would be able to' — which nobody captured as a follow-up date.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON CONFIDENCE: the recording terminates mid-exchange with the rep saying 'I lost you for a second, Robert, again' and the prospect saying 'I apologize. I lost you.' There is no close, no goodbye and no agreed next step on the recording. The disposition is inferred from four unambiguous declines, but the call did not formally end on tape and may have continued off it.
outcome.next_step: None agreed on the recording. The prospect indicated he would be able to reconsider once existing debts clear in a matter of months; no follow-up was booked before the connection dropped.

notable.note: The hardest objection handling in the batch and the one a principal most needs to see. A 62-year-old retired police officer on a self-described fixed income declined four times, was told 'Do you want me to give up on you that easily' and 'we still haven't even explored the possible options and you're declining already', was asked to disclose his savings and checking balances, refused on privacy grounds, and was then asked again with his 401k invoked. He also disclosed an L3-L4-L5 spinal fusion, a triceps tear still under investigation with a specialist appointment the next day, and prior clinical advice that his lifting days were over — and not one clearance question was asked. Two further findings: he arrived expecting the programme to cost $1,200 to $2,400, which is roughly what Primal University costs and which was never offered to him; and he handed the rep the most vivid cost-of-inaction material in the entire batch, a father who spent his last decade in a wheelchair, which was never built into a consequence frame.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion throughout, including on the most consequential lines. The rep's question 'what kind of injuries, are there any, anything that's limiting your movements?' is attached to the prospect's block; the rep's price presentation and the prospect's reaction to it alternate incorrectly around 00:38:08; and 'That's a lot of money. That's a lot more than I thought it would be' sits under the rep's label but is plainly the prospect. Both participants' names appear under the wrong labels in several exchanges. The recording is also truncated — it ends mid-objection during a connection failure with no closing exchange. Roles read from content throughout.
